course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Exercise class 3: the Corpus iuris civilis and medieval law

slides.title: The extent of Rome and why reception does not follow from it
slides.text: Roman law is the COMMON FOUNDATION OF THE CONTINENTAL EUROPEAN LEGAL CULTURES — the exercise class puts it thus: IT IS WHERE WE TAKE THE 'STRUCTURE OF LAW' AND OUR APPROACH TO ALL KINDS OF LEGAL PROBLEMS FROM. Around the turn of the era the empire stretched FROM SPAIN IN THE WEST TO PALESTINE IN THE EAST and FROM NORTH AFRICA TO ENGLAND (Hadrian's Wall); it also covered most of present-day Austria, where the DANUBE formed the 'NATURAL FRONTIER'. AND NOW THE POINT, WHICH IS ALSO THE TRAP IN THE QUESTION: THE TERRITORIAL EXTENT OF THE EMPIRE HAD NO INFLUENCE ON LATER LEGAL ORDERS — RECEPTION DECIDED. The proof is GREAT BRITAIN: it lay in the territory of the former Roman Empire, and yet COMMON LAW applies there. Where the law arrived was decided not by how far the legions reached, but by WHERE THE GRADUATES OF THE UNIVERSITIES WENT.

cards.q: Did the territorial extent of the Roman Empire decide later legal orders?
cards.a: NO — RECEPTION DECIDED. The proof is GREAT BRITAIN: it lay in the territory of the former empire and yet COMMON LAW applies there. Where the law arrived was decided not by how far the legions reached but by WHERE THE UNIVERSITY GRADUATES WENT.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: Advocate, jurist, consilium and responsum
slides.text: The exercise class distinguishes two roles that today merge into one, and that distinction is the answer to the question whether the Roman jurists were 'lawyers'. ADVOCATES (CICERO, for example) SPENT THE DAY IN COURT — speaking, persuading, representing. JURISTS (IURISTAE) WROTE LEGAL OPINIONS, and these are classified by who requested them: 'CONSILIA' drawn up AT THE REQUEST OF A PARTY and 'RESPONSA' drawn up AT THE REQUEST OF THE PRAETOR. And an addition that shows how law was thereby made: THE PRAETORS DEVELOPED THE LAW FURTHER PRECISELY ON THE BASIS OF THOSE OPINIONS. THE TWO GREAT SCHOOLS: the SABINIANS and the PROCULIANS (1st century AD). THE OLDEST ROMAN LAW the exercise names: the TWELVE TABLES (451 BC), the LEX AQUILIA (on damage) and the LEX IULIA (18 BC, Augustus's marriage legislation).

terms.def: An opinion drawn up at the request of a party × at the request of the praetor.

cards.q: How did the Roman advocate differ from the jurist, and what are consilia and responsa?
cards.a: ADVOCATES (Cicero) SPENT THE DAY IN COURT. JURISTS WROTE OPINIONS: 'CONSILIA' AT THE REQUEST OF A PARTY and 'RESPONSA' AT THE REQUEST OF THE PRAETOR. And THE PRAETORS DEVELOPED THE LAW FURTHER PRECISELY ON THE BASIS OF THOSE OPINIONS.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: Name the oldest Roman enactments according to the exercise class.
cards.a: The TWELVE TABLES (451 BC), the LEX AQUILIA (on damage) and the LEX IULIA (18 BC, Augustus's marriage legislation).
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: The Law of Citations of 426 and the unity of law after the division of the empire
slides.text: IN AD 426 A STATUTE WAS ENACTED UNDER WHICH ONLY THE TEACHINGS OF SIX JURISTS WERE LEGALLY BINDING — this is called the LAW OF CITATIONS. It is a response to an intolerable state of affairs: there was so much classical literature, and it was so contradictory, that the judge needed a rule about whose opinion prevailed. AND NOW THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ABOUT THE EFFECT OF THE DIVISION OF THE EMPIRE, WHICH RUNS AGAINST EXPECTATION: THE DIVISION OF THE EMPIRE DID NOT DISRUPT THE UNITY OF THE LAW OF THE FORMER EMPIRE — the Law of Citations, for instance, WAS ISSUED BY BOTH EMPERORS. Legislation therefore remained common even though the administration was divided. WHAT DIVERGED WERE THE FATES: THE WESTERN ROMAN EMPIRE SANK IN THE STORMS OF THE MIGRATION PERIOD, while the EASTERN ROMAN EMPIRE CONTINUED FOR ALMOST A THOUSAND YEARS AND STOOD IN THE DIRECT LEGAL TRADITION OF OLD ROME. That is why the first great collection arises there: in 438 the Byzantine emperor THEODOSIUS II had ALL THE IMPERIAL STATUTES STILL IN FORCE collected — the CODEX THEODOSIANUS.

terms.def: The statute of 426 under which only the teachings of six jurists were legally binding.

cards.q: What is the Law of Citations and why did it come about?
cards.a: A statute OF 426 under which ONLY THE TEACHINGS OF SIX JURISTS WERE LEGALLY BINDING. It came about because there was so much classical literature, and it was so CONTRADICTORY, that the judge needed a rule about WHOSE OPINION PREVAILED.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: Did the division of the empire disrupt the unity of the law?
cards.a: NO — the Law of Citations, for instance, WAS ISSUED BY BOTH EMPERORS, so legislation remained common even though the administration was divided. What diverged were the FATES: the West sank in the migration period, THE EAST CONTINUED FOR ALMOST A THOUSAND YEARS IN THE DIRECT LEGAL TRADITION OF ROME — which is why the CODEX THEODOSIANUS (438) arises there.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: Why the Digest came about and why the Institutes were needed alongside it
slides.text: The Byzantine emperor JUSTINIAN I (527–565) SOUGHT TO RESTORE THE ROMAN EMPIRE, and his codification is part of that programme. IN 529 he issued a CODE similar to the Codex Theodosianus. AT THE SAME TIME HE APPOINTED A COMMISSION TO COLLECT, EDIT AND PUBLISH THE CLASSICAL JURISTIC WRITINGS — thus arose the DIGEST or PANDECTS: FIFTY BOOKS, that is, extracts from the original texts of the late classical jurists BROUGHT INTO A SYSTEMATIC ORDER. And an important qualification the exercise class states expressly: THE TEXTS IN THE DIGEST WERE ALTERED IN LINE WITH THE LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE TIME IN ORDER TO 'MODERNIZE' THEM. They are therefore not a faithful imprint of the classical texts — and uncovering those alterations (interpolations) will later be the work of the humanists. WHY THE INSTITUTES CAME ABOUT: because THE DIGEST DID NOT EXPLAIN IMPORTANT BASIC CONCEPTS and lacked ABSTRACT PROPOSITIONS. Justinian therefore launched the project of a TEXTBOOK THAT WOULD HELP IN UNDERSTANDING THE DIGEST — the INSTITUTIONES were to serve as an INTRODUCTION TO ROMAN LAW. And a distinction worth remembering, because it runs against expectation: THE DIGEST IS THE LAW BOOK WITH THE GREATEST IMPACT ON EUROPEAN LEGAL CULTURE (through reception) — BUT BOTH THE FRENCH CODE CIVIL (1804) AND THE AUSTRIAN ABGB (1811) FOLLOW THE SYSTEM OF THE INSTITUTES, NOT OF THE DIGEST. The content thus came from the Digest, the arrangement from the textbook. The NOVELLAE are the statutes enacted AFTER 533 and APPENDED to the CIC.

cards.q: How did the Digest come about and what is essential about its text?
cards.a: Justinian appointed a commission TO COLLECT, EDIT AND PUBLISH THE CLASSICAL JURISTIC WRITINGS — FIFTY BOOKS of extracts brought into a SYSTEMATIC ORDER. What is essential is that THE TEXTS WERE ALTERED IN LINE WITH THE LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE TIME IN ORDER TO 'MODERNIZE' THEM — they are therefore no faithful imprint of the classical texts, and uncovering those INTERPOLATIONS will be the work of the humanists.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: Why did the Institutiones come about and how does that show in the modern codes?
cards.a: Because THE DIGEST DID NOT EXPLAIN THE BASIC CONCEPTS and lacked ABSTRACT PROPOSITIONS — the Institutes were to be an INTRODUCTION helping to understand the Digest. And the point: THE DIGEST HAD THE GREATEST IMPACT through reception, BUT BOTH THE CODE CIVIL (1804) AND THE ABGB (1811) FOLLOW THE SYSTEM OF THE INSTITUTES. Content from the Digest, arrangement from the textbook.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: Graeca non leguntur: why it concerns the Novels in particular
slides.text: The exercise class gives a simple and precise explanation here, which is useful to have at hand. THE NOVELLAE, THAT IS, THE STATUTES ENACTED AFTER 533 AND APPENDED TO THE CIC, WERE WRITTEN IN GREEK — Justinian ruled a Greek-speaking empire and stopped using Latin for new enactments. BUT AT THE TIME OF THE RECEPTION IN THE MIDDLE AGES THE PREDOMINANT LANGUAGE IN ACADEMIC CIRCLES WAS LATIN. THE CONSEQUENCE: ONLY THE LATIN PARTS OF THE CORPUS IURIS BECAME THE BASIS OF THE IUS COMMUNE — hence the maxim 'GRAECA NON LEGUNTUR'. It is therefore not a mere curiosity: IT DECIDED WHICH PART OF JUSTINIAN'S WORK BECAME LIVING LAW IN EUROPE AND WHICH WAS LEFT ASIDE.

cards.q: Why does 'Graeca non leguntur' concern the Novels in particular, and what followed from it?
cards.a: The NOVELLAE, the statutes enacted AFTER 533, WERE WRITTEN IN GREEK (Justinian ruled a Greek-speaking empire). At the time of the reception, however, the PREDOMINANT ACADEMIC LANGUAGE WAS LATIN, so ONLY THE LATIN PARTS OF THE CIC BECAME THE BASIS OF THE IUS COMMUNE. It decided WHICH PART OF JUSTINIAN'S WORK BECAME LIVING LAW IN EUROPE.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: Leges barbarorum as a mixture, not Germanic law
slides.text: Here the exercise class corrects a widespread notion. WHEN THE GERMANIC PRINCES FIRST ENCOUNTERED THE ROMAN EMPIRE AND ITS LAW, CLASSICAL ROMAN LAW WAS ALREADY IN DECLINE; from the early Middle Ages it was simplified more and more, which led 19th-century legal historians to the label 'VULGAR LAW'. The LEGES BARBARORUM are the GERMANIC LAWS RECORDED BY GERMANIC KINGS BETWEEN 500 AND 800. AND NOW THE CORRECTION: IT WAS NOT PURELY ORIGINAL GERMANIC LAW BUT THE PRODUCT OF A FUSION OF GERMANIC AND OLD ROMAN CULTURE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF CHRISTIANITY. The exercise gives one concrete and very telling piece of evidence: THE PROHIBITION OF EXPOSING OR KILLING NEWBORN CHILDREN — that is neither a Germanic custom nor a Roman tradition but a Christian intervention. THE LAST of all the leges barbarorum is the LEX SAXONUM OF 802. AND THE IMPACT BY REGION: THEY HAD LITTLE INFLUENCE ON AUSTRIA, because there the law of the Germanic tribes remained customary; THEY HAD GREAT INFLUENCE, by contrast, IN SPAIN, ITALY AND SOUTHERN FRANCE.

cards.q: Are the leges barbarorum purely Germanic law?
cards.a: NO. They are laws recorded by Germanic kings BETWEEN 500 AND 800, but they are the PRODUCT OF A FUSION OF GERMANIC AND OLD ROMAN CULTURE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF CHRISTIANITY. Concrete evidence: THE PROHIBITION OF EXPOSING OR KILLING NEWBORN CHILDREN — neither a Germanic custom nor a Roman tradition but a CHRISTIAN INTERVENTION.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: Which statute is the last of the leges barbarorum and where did they have the greatest influence?
cards.a: The LEX SAXONUM OF 802. They had great influence in SPAIN, ITALY AND SOUTHERN FRANCE; on AUSTRIA, by contrast, LITTLE, because there the law of the Germanic tribes remained CUSTOMARY.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: The Sachsenspiegel, the two-emperor problem and the relation of pope and emperor
slides.text: To the Sachsenspiegel the exercise class adds three things. (1) ITS NATURE: IT WAS NOT A STATUTE BUT A 'MIRROR' OF SAXON CUSTOMARY LAW — a record of custom, not actual legislation, and yet SOME PARTS OPERATED AS ACTUAL LAW. It is an AUTHENTIC PICTURE OF CUSTOMARY LAW IN THE MIDDLE AGES. (2) THE AUTHOR: EIKE VON REPGOW, WHO SERVED AT A BISHOP'S COURT AND WAS EDUCATED IN A MONASTERY SCHOOL, NOT AT A UNIVERSITY — a detail that matters, because it explains why his text is not a learned work of Roman law but a record of native law. (3) THE IMPACT: GREAT, AND NOT ONLY FOR SAXONY BUT FROM THE NETHERLANDS TO UKRAINE; HUNDREDS OF MANUSCRIPTS survive and the text was in part IN USE UNTIL THE 20TH CENTURY. THE TWO-EMPEROR PROBLEM (Zweikaiserproblem) is the dispute arising because TWO POWERS SIMULTANEOUSLY CLAIMED THE TITLE OF ROMAN EMPEROR — the Byzantine emperor in the east, who regarded himself as the unbroken continuation of Rome, and the Roman-German emperor in the west from the coronation of Charlemagne in 800. A universal claim, however, by its very nature tolerates only one bearer, which is why the dispute was insoluble. THE RELATION OF POPE AND EMPEROR IN THE MIDDLE AGES: according to the Sachsenspiegel the EMPEROR AND THE POPE WERE OF THE SAME ORDER, AND THE SPIRITUAL AND TEMPORAL SPHERES EVENTUALLY SEPARATED — and the exercise adds the comparison that is the core of the whole question: THIS IS A PECULIARITY OF THE CATHOLIC CHURCH; IN ISLAM IT IS NOT SO, because there the caliph unites both in one person.

terms.def: Two powers simultaneously claimed the title of Roman emperor — the Byzantine and the Roman-German; but a universal claim tolerates only one bearer.

cards.q: What is the nature of the Sachsenspiegel and who was its author?
cards.a: IT WAS NOT A STATUTE but a 'MIRROR' OF SAXON CUSTOMARY LAW — a record of custom, and yet some parts operated as actual law; it is an AUTHENTIC PICTURE of customary law. The author is EIKE VON REPGOW, who served at a bishop's court and WAS EDUCATED IN A MONASTERY SCHOOL, NOT AT A UNIVERSITY — which is why it is not a learned work of Roman law.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: What impact did the Sachsenspiegel have?
cards.a: GREAT, and NOT ONLY FOR SAXONY BUT FROM THE NETHERLANDS TO UKRAINE; HUNDREDS OF MANUSCRIPTS survive and the text was in part IN USE UNTIL THE 20TH CENTURY.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: What is the two-emperor problem and what was the relation of pope and emperor?
cards.a: THE TWO-EMPEROR PROBLEM: TWO POWERS SIMULTANEOUSLY CLAIMED the title of Roman emperor — the Byzantine emperor as the unbroken continuation of Rome and the Roman-German emperor from 800; but a universal claim tolerates only one bearer. THE EMPEROR AND THE POPE WERE OF THE SAME ORDER and the spiritual and temporal spheres eventually SEPARATED — which is a PECULIARITY OF THE CATHOLIC CHURCH; IN ISLAM IT IS NOT SO.

slides.title: Universities as corporations, and foundation for political reasons
slides.text: On universities the exercise class gives two things that are not found elsewhere. (1) WHAT A UNIVERSITY ORIGINALLY IS: the growing influx of students from the 11TH CENTURY led to the founding of 'COMMUNITIES OF TEACHERS AND STUDENTS' — 'UNIVERSITATES MAGISTRORUM ET SCHOLARIUM'. The word 'university' therefore originally means neither a building nor a discipline but a CORPORATION, that is, a legal person; and it was precisely as a corporation that it secured privileges, its own jurisdiction over its members and independence. (2) TWO WAVES OF FOUNDATION: first the 11TH CENTURY BOLOGNA and the 13TH CENTURY PARIS (the SORBONNE), which arose from below, out of the influx of students. Then FOUNDATION FOR POLITICAL REASONS, that is, by the decision of a ruler: 1348 PRAGUE, 1364 CRACOW, 1365 VIENNA. That difference is useful in the exam: THE OLD UNIVERSITIES CAME INTO BEING OF THEMSELVES; THE CENTRAL EUROPEAN ONES WERE FOUNDED AS AN INSTRUMENT OF TERRITORIAL POLITICS — the ruler wanted his own educated officials and not to have to send them to Italy.

cards.q: What does the word 'university' originally mean and why does that matter?
cards.a: 'UNIVERSITAS MAGISTRORUM ET SCHOLARIUM' — A COMMUNITY OF TEACHERS AND STUDENTS. It therefore means neither a building nor a discipline but a CORPORATION, a legal person — and it was precisely as a corporation that the university secured PRIVILEGES, ITS OWN JURISDICTION OVER ITS MEMBERS AND INDEPENDENCE.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

cards.q: Which two waves of university foundation does the exercise class distinguish?
cards.a: 1) ARISING FROM BELOW out of the influx of students: 11TH CENTURY BOLOGNA, 13TH CENTURY PARIS (the Sorbonne). 2) FOUNDATION FOR POLITICAL REASONS by a ruler's decision: 1348 PRAGUE, 1364 CRACOW, 1365 VIENNA — the ruler wanted HIS OWN EDUCATED OFFICIALS and not to have to send them to Italy.
cards.topic: Development of Law in the Middle Ages

slides.title: Reception as the academization of practice, not the transfer of a text
slides.text: The exercise class gives a definition more precise than the usual one. 'RECEPTION' DESCRIBES THE TRANSFER OF THE RESULTS OF LEGISTICS FROM THE UNIVERSITIES INTO LEGAL PRACTICE. It is a PAN-EUROPEAN PROCESS THAT BEGAN IN THE 13TH CENTURY, the trigger being the REDISCOVERY OF A MANUSCRIPT OF THE DIGEST — the 'CODEX FLORENTINUS' — AROUND 1155. It gave rise to a pan-European law, the IUS COMMUNE. AND NOW THE KEY SENTENCE: RECEPTION DID NOT TAKE PLACE AS A 'DIRECT TRANSFER' OF ROMAN LAW BUT AS THE GRADUAL ACADEMIZATION OF LEGAL PRACTICE — the graduates of the law schools (Pavia, Bologna) were increasingly employed in the JUDICIARY, THE ADMINISTRATION AND POLITICS. Nobody, then, issued a decree that Roman law henceforth applied; the people who make the law were simply gradually replaced. The legal scholarship of the time consisted of CANONISTICS AND LEGISTICS; FROM THE 12TH/13TH CENTURY learned jurists serve NORTH OF THE ALPS as well, as JUDGES, ADVOCATES OR LEGAL ADVISERS TO PRINCES AND CITIES. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES: in the HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE the reception was STRONG IN SCHOLARSHIP, PRACTICE AND LEGISLATION ALIKE. IN ENGLAND IT WAS WEAK, and the exercise gives the reason: A STRONG GOVERNMENT WITH A STRONG ROYAL JUDICIARY — THE COURTS BRIDGED THE REGIONAL DIFFERENCES AND DEVELOPED A LAW COMMON TO ENGLAND. That is: England had its own solution to the same problem before the reception arrived. THE LAW BOOK ON WHICH A STRONG RECEPTION IS VISIBLE is, according to the exercise, the 'SIETE PARTIDAS' (13th century), which MERGES CUSTOMARY AND ROMAN LAW and interprets custom in the light of Roman law — evidence of a strong reception in SPAIN.

terms.def: The manuscript of the Digest rediscovered around 1155; the trigger of the reception.

cards.q: How does the exercise class define reception, and what exactly was it?
cards.a: As the TRANSFER OF THE RESULTS OF LEGISTICS FROM THE UNIVERSITIES INTO LEGAL PRACTICE, a pan-European process from the 13th century, triggered by the REDISCOVERY OF A MANUSCRIPT OF THE DIGEST (the 'CODEX FLORENTINUS') AROUND 1155. The key point: IT DID NOT TAKE PLACE AS A 'DIRECT TRANSFER' OF LAW BUT AS THE GRADUAL ACADEMIZATION OF LEGAL PRACTICE — graduates were increasingly employed in the judiciary, the administration and politics.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: Why was the reception weak in England, and which book attests a strong reception in Spain?
cards.a: England had a STRONG GOVERNMENT WITH A STRONG ROYAL JUDICIARY — THE COURTS BRIDGED THE REGIONAL DIFFERENCES AND DEVELOPED A COMMON LAW before the reception arrived. A strong reception in Spain is attested by the SIETE PARTIDAS (13th century), which MERGE CUSTOMARY AND ROMAN LAW and interpret custom in the light of Roman law.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The glossators: scholasticism without source criticism
slides.text: The exercise class gives the glossators one characterization that is at the same time a criticism, and it is worth knowing verbatim. THE GLOSSATORS WERE THE FIRST JURISTS OF THE MIDDLE AGES and wrote 'GLOSSES', that is, EXPLANATORY NOTES, on the Corpus iuris. THE METHOD THEY USED WAS SCHOLASTIC — AND WITHOUT SOURCE CRITICISM. THEY SOUGHT EXCLUSIVELY TO REMOVE INCONSISTENCIES AND CONTRADICTIONS. That means two things: they took the text as an AUTHORITY THAT CANNOT BE INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY, and therefore regarded every contradiction as APPARENT, to be removed by interpretation — instead of asking whether the text might be corrupt, later, or internally heterogeneous. It is precisely this blind spot that the humanists will later hold against them. THE COMMENTATORS are the SUCCESSORS OF THE GLOSSATORS IN THE LATE 13TH CENTURY and write COMMENTARIES AND CONSILIA, that is, opinions. The difference is therefore one of genre as well: A GLOSS IS A NOTE ON A TEXT, A CONSILIUM IS AN OPINION ON A CASE.

cards.q: What method did the glossators use and what is its blind spot?
cards.a: THE SCHOLASTIC METHOD — AND WITHOUT SOURCE CRITICISM; they sought exclusively to REMOVE INCONSISTENCIES AND CONTRADICTIONS. They took the text as an AUTHORITY THAT CANNOT BE INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY, so every contradiction was treated as APPARENT — instead of asking whether the text might be corrupt, later, or heterogeneous. Precisely this the humanists will hold against them.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: What is the difference of genre between the glossators and the commentators?
cards.a: A GLOSS IS A NOTE ON A TEXT, A CONSILIUM IS AN OPINION ON A CASE. The commentators are the successors of the glossators in the LATE 13TH CENTURY and write COMMENTARIES AND CONSILIA.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

slides.title: The subsidiarity of the ius commune and the burden of proof
slides.text: Here the exercise class formulates the rule more precisely than it is usually stated, and the difference is legally essential. The IUS COMMUNE is the COMMON LAW, that is, the LEARNED LAWS — Roman and canon; 'common' is said here in opposition to 'PARTICULAR', that is, to the local or native laws, the IURA PARTICULARIA. It had a UNIVERSAL character because IT WAS TIED NEITHER TO A PARTICULAR TERRITORY NOR TO A PARTICULAR GROUP OF PEOPLE. AND NOW THE RULE: THE IUS COMMUNE WAS APPLIED SUBSIDIARILY, THAT IS, WHERE THE EXISTENCE OF A CONFLICTING LOCAL CUSTOM COULD NOT BE PROVED. Note that this is not phrased as 'where the local law is silent' but as a BURDEN OF PROOF: it is not that the local law does not apply, but that IT MUST BE PROVED — and whoever fails to prove it is judged by the learned law. It is precisely this procedural form of subsidiarity that explains why the reception prevailed in practice: it did not have to abolish anything, it was enough that it was the DEFAULT POSITION.

cards.q: How exactly does the rule on the subsidiarity of the ius commune run, and why does the phrasing matter?
cards.a: THE IUS COMMUNE APPLIED WHERE THE EXISTENCE OF A CONFLICTING LOCAL CUSTOM COULD NOT BE PROVED. It is therefore not 'where the local law is silent' but a BURDEN OF PROOF: the local law applies, but IT MUST BE PROVED. Precisely this procedural form explains why the reception prevailed — it did not have to abolish anything, it was enough that it was the DEFAULT POSITION.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times

cards.q: Why did the ius commune have a universal character?
cards.a: Because IT WAS TIED NEITHER TO A PARTICULAR TERRITORY NOR TO A PARTICULAR GROUP OF PEOPLE — unlike the iura particularia, the local and native laws.
cards.topic: The Ius Commune and the Early Modern Times
